newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Dozens of Israelis die when army copters collide.
newsitem.headline: Dozens of Israelis die when army copters collide.

text.p: Dozens of Israeli soldiers were killed when two military helicopters collided in mid-air in a storm in northern Israel on Tuesday evening, military sources said.
Security sources described the two helicopters as American-made Sikorsky CH-53 transporters, each holding 37 people on their way to an Israeli-held south Lebanon occupation zone.
David Bar-Illan, a spokesman for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, said it was doubtful any passengers survived. Military sources said only that dozens were killed.
He told the BBC World Service Television it was "as great a disaster as anything in recent years".
The crash occurred around 7 p.m. (1700 GMT).
Netanyahu cancelled a trip to Jordan planned for Wednesday.
"I saw about 30 bodies on the ground. Some had their legs cut off. There were some in civilian clothes. They were all lined up by the side of the road," a witness said.
"Two helicopters of the air force crashed this evening in Shaar Yishuv in the Galilee Panhandle," the army said in its first terse announcement.

The Galilee Panhandle is perhaps best known to the world as the target of Katyusha rockets fired by Arab guerrillas from Lebanon. Shaar Yishuv is situated near the northern Israeli settlement of Kiryat Shmona.

Military censors held up publication of the report for two hours in an effort first to notify families. But the sheer size of the disaster made keeping it secret impossible in a country where news travels fast.

"We went outside and we saw a helicopter hang in the air and then fall on the bungalows near our house," resident Sylvia Cohen said. "I went outside and saw soldiers on the ground. I tried to resuscitate one of them. It was a terrible sight."
Another witness, a man, told reporters: "There was clearly some problem that it simply sounded as if something was about to happen."

Military helicopters circled overhead immediately after the crash, witnesses said. They said wreckage fell on bugalows in the farming community and at least one caught fire but police said it was unclear if any residents were killed.
About 1,000 Israeli soldiers patrol a 15 km (nine mile)-wide occupation zone in south Lebanon carved out in 1985 to prevent guerrilla attacks on the Jewish state's northern border.

A resident of the area said there were explosions after the crash, apparently caused by ammunition in the cargo. He said no one was hurt from Shaar Yishuv although the helicopters crashed into bungalows.
Rescue workers evacuated dozens of bodies on stretchers after the crash.

"This is an unimaginably heavy tragedy. The hearts of the nation are with the victims. The whole country weeps today over the loss of these young fighters," Netanyahu said in a statement issued by his office.
